sentence: This project develops methods that forecast how infectious diseases spread, plan interventions to control them, and monitor populations using clinical reports and wastewater signals.
This project develops computational methods that combine cryo-electron tomography and fluorescence microscopy to learn which proteins are in different cell structures.
This project develops learning modules that help researchers learn to use Cloud DevOps tools for modernizing scientific workflows.
This project designs, synthesizes and studies materials where the crystal structure shapes the interplay between charge and spin.
This project develops a computational tool that uses physical models to predict how strongly antibodies and antigens bind, for faster immunoassay development.
This project uses advanced computing to study problems such as turbulent fluid flows, properties of porous material, and bias in machine learning models.
This project develops an integrated hardware device that filters out interference in real-time, letting commercial and government users share spectrum.
This project compares statistical methods for modeling how weather affects the survival, reproduction and population growth of multiple plant species.
This project studies the genetic interplay between a bacterium that causes wilt disease and cucumber and melon plants, looking for natural resistance and disease genes.
This project improves predictive computer models of how fish and other animals that live in water use energy under stress, such as catch-and-release fishing.
This project tries to find out why some soil bacteria thrive after wildfires, using field research, laboratory experiments and genetic sequencing.
This project studies how a copper-based ferritin protein affects iron storage in phytoplankton and the dissolved iron in the ocean.
This project develops genetic analysis tools that use molecular and cellular biology knowledge in statistical models to map genes and predict traits.
This conference covers the molecular and cellular processes that govern plant cell architecture, polarity, division and intracellular trafficking.
This project studies how rural contexts shape engineering pathways, identity and belonging, using site visits, interviews and a survey.
This project develops solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance methods that reveal the atomic-level structure of formulated pharmaceuticals.
This project develops a framework that explains why language models of source code make the predictions they do.
This project develops models and algorithms that let robots manipulate deformable objects by integrating sight and touch.
This study tries to find out how motor proteins make the antenna of the fruit fly move actively to tune and amplify auditory sensitivity.
